questions.prompt: What is the cleanest way to make clock-reading code testable?

options.text: Call datetime.now() inside the function and hope for the best
Inject `now` as a parameter so the test supplies a fixed value
Only run the test at noon

questions.explanation: Injecting the time makes the dependency explicit and lets the test control it, avoiding wall-clock flakiness.

questions.prompt: Does a test that passes with a fixed random seed prove the code is correct for all inputs?

options.text: Yes, a seed covers every case
No — it only pins that one draw; broad input coverage needs property-based testing

questions.explanation: A seed makes one draw reproducible; verifying behavior across many inputs is the job of property-based testing.

questions.prompt: Which techniques keep time/randomness tests deterministic? Select all that apply.

options.text: Freeze the clock with freeze_time when you can't inject
Use real time.sleep to wait out backoff delays
Use a library seed knob like random_state

questions.explanation: Injected/seeded randomness and frozen clocks give determinism; real sleeps just make tests slow and flaky.

questions.prompt: To test exponential backoff instantly, inject the ____ function and assert the wait durations instead of actually waiting.
questions.explanation: Injecting (or recording) the sleep lets you verify the backoff schedule without real delays.

questions.prompt: Match each need to a suitable technique.

pairs.right: Inject or record sleep; fake clock
Await the real condition, not a fixed sleep

questions.explanation: Each need maps to a determinism-preserving approach rather than real time or unseeded randomness.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to make a token generator that uses time and randomness testable.

items.text: Change the function to accept now and an rng parameter
In the test, pass a fixed datetime and a seeded Random
Assert the exact expiry and value produced

questions.explanation: Inject the sources, supply fixed values in the test, then assert the fully-determined output.
